text:
maria: Seeing lots of reports from canary that Dashboard charts are stuttering on first interaction after the new prefetch priority patch. Users in eu-west show 200-500ms frame drops.
ajay: thanks — do we have a repro and a trace? Haven't seen it locally.
sam: repro in staging, can hit it on heatmap with ~50k rows. Looks like chunk decode + kvcache miss thrash. stack trace points to ChartRenderer.hydrate() blocking main thread.
olivia: :thinking_face: our prefetch changed priorities to deprioritize chart assets for background tabs — could that have regressed initial paint when route switches quickly?
maria: exact change was to reduce prefetch parallelism and add an affinity slot per route. aim was to reduce bundle duplication across panes.
zach: deploy-bot: canary deployed revision r-2026.03.21-17
nora: telemetry shows a jump in main-thread parse time coincident with the deploy. avg main-thread parse went from 22ms -> 88ms for first paint on metric-pane.
ajay: interesting. can you paste the perf snippet?

nora: ```
main_thread_parse_ms: before: 22
main_thread_parse_ms: after: 88
kvcache_hit_rate: before: 0.83
kvcache_hit_rate: after: 0.64
bundle_bytes_requested: +45KB per route
```
sam: that lower kvcache hit rate smells like keying mismatch after we changed route->cache keying to include prefetched chunk list.
olivia: hmm we added route fingerprinting to avoid stale widgets across routes. If fingerprint changes on nav, cached prefix is invalidated and we fall back to full parse.
maria: so prefetch reductions + fingerprinting = double whammy: fewer parallel downloads and more cache misses = bursts of parse on main thread.
ajay: agrees. two mitigation options: 1) revert fingerprinting until we can be smarter about stable keys, or 2) keep fingerprinting but make prefetch more aggressive for initial route transitions (temporary boost for canary users).
zach: deploy-bot: canary traffic is ~2.4% of prod. we can patch quickly if we pick option 2.
olivia: prefer option 2 short-term. it's safer than reverting a correctness fix that prevented widget bleed.
sam: quick patch proposal: when nav.type === 'user-initiated' and route_latency < 200ms, set prefetchParallelism = 6 and warm KVCACHE with prefix-only fetch for top-3 chart chunks. Code:

```js
if (nav.userInitiated && route.latency < 200) {
  prefetch.parallel = 6;
  prefetch.warmPrefixes = topChunks.slice(0,3);
}
```
ajay: need to ensure we don't blow network budget. this will increase token bytes for small % of requests. we should gate by plan tier to respect quotas.
maria: good call. add gating: only for enterprise and internal testing buckets.
nora: telemetry change req: add an event prefetch.override={strategy:"boosted-prefix", reason:"post-canary-stall"} so we can correlate.
zach: i'll stage a hotfix branch and run a 1% canary with boosted prefix + enterprise gating.
olivia: can we also add a guard to avoid invalidating kvcache on minor fingerprint deltas? maybe a fuzzy match or drop sequence numbers from the fingerprint.
ajay: prefer to roll the fuzzy keying as a follow-up. not safe to do in hotfix. tech debt ticket created.

maria: action items:
- zach: hotfix branch + 1% boosted-prefix canary (ETA 2h)
- nora: add telemetry event and dashboard panel for boosted-prefix correlation (ETA 3h)
- sam: instrument kvcache key distribution and add fuzz-match ticket (ETA EOD)
- olivia: draft short incident note for customers on canary impact (ETA 1h)

zach: starting branch now. will post the PR shortly.
ajay: thanks all. if metrics don't improve in 4h we revert the canary.
maria: :thumbsup: update here when PR links are up.
